free_tier.stated: Not a storage candidate at all: the AUR enforces a hard maximum blob size of 250 KiB per git object. The git hook rejects the push: 'remote: error: maximum blob size (250.00KiB) exceeded / remote: error: hook declined to update refs/heads/master'. Config files around 250.8 KiB already trip it.

retention.stated: per-object-cap: 250 KiB (hard, server-side git hook). retention: indefinite for packages

egress.terms: Free (plain git over SSH/HTTPS), but irrelevant given the cap.

record.tooling: git over ssh://aur.archlinux.org/<pkg>.git; AUR RPC v5 at /rpc/. No rclone backend (git is the interface).
record.chaining: unlimited AUR packages x 250 KiB = useless for bulk. Content must be PKGBUILD + patches; large sources are fetched at build time by URL, never stored.
record.limits_note: per-object-cap: 250 KiB (hard, server-side git hook). retention: indefinite for packages. request-rate: git push over ssh, per-key.
record.reliability_note: Any 'AUR as storage' idea dies here.

evidence.proved: 'remote: error: maximum blob size (250.00KiB) exceeded' on a 250.8 KiB config file; maintainer confirms the limit is intentional
probe: GET -> 200, 679 bytes (RPC v5 live; metadata only, no blob path)
